Traditional library management systems primarily focus on functions such as book cataloging, issuing, returning, and maintaining records. However, these systems often rely on keyword-based searches and lack intelligent features such as personalized recommendations, natural language interaction, and efficient retrieval of digital resources. This limits users' ability to quickly discover relevant books and research materials.

The implemented project, LuminaR – AI-Powered Library Management System, aims to modernize conventional library services by integrating Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing (NLP). The system will incorporate a fine-tuned domain-specific Mini LLM based on a pre-trained Transformer model to enable semantic search, personalized book recommendations, conversational assistance, intelligent document summarization, and question answering over digital resources. Additionally, the system will support AI-based metadata management and analytics to enhance library operations and improve user experience.

The application will be developed using React for the frontend, FastAPI for the backend, DuckDB and SQLite for database management, and PyTorch with Hugging Face Transformers for fine-tuning the language model. By combining modern web technologies with domain-specific AI capabilities, LuminaR aims to provide an intelligent, scalable, and user-friendly library ecosystem that enhances learning, simplifies information retrieval, and supports efficient library management.

Libraries are essential for providing access to knowledge and educational resources. Traditional library management systems mainly focus on cataloging books, issuing and returning materials, and keeping records. While these systems automate administrative tasks, they usually depend on keyword-based search methods and offer limited support for personalized recommendations and smart information retrieval.

The growing availability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) technologies offers a chance to change conventional library systems into smart digital platforms. The proposed project, LuminaR, is an AI-Powered Library Management System that includes AI-driven features like semantic search, personalized recommendations, conversational assistance, intelligent metadata management, and research paper support. The system aims to improve the library experience by helping users find relevant learning resources more efficiently and assisting librarians in managing resources effectively.

This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document outlines the functional and non-functional requirements of the LuminaR, an AI-Powered Library Management System. It serves as a guide for developers, project supervisors, testers, and stakeholders. The document offers a clear understanding of the system's goals, architecture, features, and operational needs. It also lays the groundwork for system design, implementation, testing, and future improvements.

LuminaR is an implemented web-based library management system powered by AI. It simplifies managing and accessing books, e-books, journals, and research papers for students, faculty, researchers, librarians, administrators, and general readers. The system includes key library management features such as user management, book catalog management, handling book issuance and returns, managing reservations, tracking fines, and monitoring inventory.

Beyond these traditional features, LuminaR uses artificial intelligence to offer improved capabilities. These include semantic search, personalized resource recommendations, an AI-powered chat assistant, smart metadata management, document summarization, and answering questions about digital resources. The system employs a fine-tuned, domain-specific Mini Large Language Model based on a pre-trained Transformer architecture. This allows for better context-aware interactions and enhances information retrieval.

Additionally, the system provides analytical insights and reporting tools to help librarians with resource planning, collection management, and decision-making. LuminaR seeks to improve the library experience by enabling faster discovery of resources, boosting user engagement, minimizing manual effort, and delivering a smart, scalable, and user-friendly platform for modern library services.

LuminaR is an AI-powered web-based Library Management System designed to modernize traditional library operations by integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Machine Learning (ML) technologies with conventional library management functionalities. The system aims to simplify the management and accessibility of books, e-books, journals, and research papers while providing intelligent services that enhance user experience and improve library operations.

Unlike traditional library management systems that primarily rely on keyword-based searches and manual resource management, LuminaR introduces AI-powered capabilities such as semantic search, personalized recommendations, conversational assistance, intelligent metadata management, document summarization, and research paper question answering. These features are supported by a fine-tuned, domain-specific Mini Large Language Model (Mini LLM) built upon a pre-trained Transformer architecture.

The application follows a microservices-based architecture where FastAPI manages the core library operations and business logic, while a dedicated FastAPI-based AI service handles intelligent functionalities. This separation improves scalability, maintainability, and allows independent development of AI components without affecting the core library system.

The proposed system is intended for educational institutions, universities, public libraries, research organizations, and digital libraries, providing an intelligent platform that improves resource discovery, reduces manual workload, and supports data-driven decision making.

LuminaR is a standalone AI-powered web application that extends the capabilities of traditional library management systems. Existing systems generally provide functionalities such as user management, catalog maintenance, book circulation, inventory management, and fine calculation. Although these systems automate administrative tasks, they often lack intelligent resource discovery, personalized recommendations, natural language interaction, and automated document understanding.

The proposed system overcomes these limitations by integrating AI services into conventional library workflows. LuminaR combines standard library management functionalities with advanced AI capabilities including semantic search, conversational assistance, recommendation systems, intelligent metadata extraction, and research paper analysis.

LuminaR implements an AI-assisted discovery and document-intelligence layer alongside the core library API. The AI functions are exposed through dedicated services and are integrated into the React client through HTTP APIs.

Natural-language search is supported through the search service. Queries are normalized, represented as embeddings, matched against the indexed catalogue corpus with FAISS, and returned with relevance metadata. The search interface supports keyword and semantic discovery, result filtering, availability information, ratings, and resource navigation.

The recommendation service returns personalized or fallback recommendations. Recommendations use catalogue metadata, interaction signals, ratings, availability, and similarity information. The interface exposes recommendation explanations and gracefully falls back to popular or available resources when a user has insufficient history.

The AI assistant is available from the web application as a conversational widget and as a dedicated document-intelligence workspace. It supports library-service questions, resource discovery, recommendations, summaries, and questions over supported documents. Conversation state is maintained in the client session and service responses are presented with loading, error, and retry states.

Digital resources are processed through text extraction and retrieval workflows. PDF processing uses PyMuPDF. Text is divided into retrievable chunks, embeddings are generated with sentence-transformer tooling, and vector indexes are stored for semantic retrieval. Unsupported or invalid files are rejected by the processing workflow.

The implemented system uses relational and analytical storage rather than relying on a single database technology. Operational records are stored through the application database services, while DuckDB and Parquet datasets support catalogue, metadata, analytics, and retrieval workloads. FAISS indexes store vector representations for semantic search. The system separates catalogue works, editions, authors, covers, reading activity, inventory, users, issues, reservations, fines, and audit activity.

Notifications and email integration use the Brevo client where configured.

The FastAPI application exposes authentication, staff, books, document intelligence, issues, reservations, fines, activity, reading-list, and inventory routers. The root and health endpoints expose service identity and readiness information. Cross-origin configuration supports the Vite development client on localhost ports 3000 and 5173.

Testing combines unit tests, route and access-control tests, retrieval regression tests, AI evaluation reports, backend integration checks, and frontend build validation. Implemented test coverage includes authentication, staff access, general-user routing, read-now navigation, book access control, dynamic book capabilities, intent extraction, adversarial intent cases, query types, RAG decoding, RAG attention, metadata text, and Brevo integration. Production-style benchmarks evaluate retrieval quality, latency, embedding models, reranking, and end-to-end generation.

The frontend displays loading, empty, error, retry, success, and warning states. Authentication expiry clears local user data and redirects the user through the session flow. The backend provides health reporting, structured route separation, input validation through Pydantic, and activity records for important operations.
LuminaR: The implemented AI-powered library management system.
RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, in which retrieved library content supplies context for an AI response.
FAISS: A vector similarity-search library used by the semantic retrieval pipeline.
DuckDB: An analytical database used with catalogue, metadata, and dataset workflows.
Semantic Search: Search that uses vector representations to match the meaning and context of a query.
Reading List: A user-managed collection of saved resources.
Reservation: A request that places a user in a queue for an unavailable resource.
Fine: A monetary or policy record created for an overdue circulation item.

The implementation is based on the project source code, route modules, frontend tests, backend tests, retrieval evaluation reports, dataset pipeline scripts, and dependency manifests stored in the LuminaR project repository.
